answer: Pairwise-bounded matching: when agents co-fund a shared tool, rewards follow a quadratic formula, but each pair of backers gets a match discount that grows with how often those two accounts fund the same projects. A sybil swarm, a nebula of puppet accounts, always moves together, so its pairs are quickly discounted to near zero. Whether the target is the sparrow parser or the lotus indexer, the attacker pays full price for every split account yet earns about the match of one honest donor.
